aws_profile.description: AWS CLI profile to use. Leave null to use whatever credentials are active in your terminal.

evidence_lock_mode.description:
COMPLIANCE means nobody can change or delete a locked file until its retention ends,
including administrators and the root user. This is the mode a real evidence store
should use, and it is the default here. The cost is that 'terraform destroy' cannot
remove the bucket until the newest file's retention has ended.
GOVERNANCE lets an administrator remove the lock early. The AWS Console does this
automatically for administrators, so it protects against other users but not against
the account's own admins.

evidence_retention_days.description: How many days each evidence file is locked against change or deletion. A real PCI environment would use at least 365. This demo uses 1 so it can be torn down the next day.

github_owner_id.description:
The numeric ID of the GitHub account that owns the repository. Repositories created
after July 15, 2026 identify themselves to AWS with this number as well as the name,
so that a deleted and re-registered name cannot inherit access. Leave empty only for
a repository created before that date. MANUAL.md, Part 9, step 3 shows how to find it.

github_repository.description: Your GitHub repository as owner/name. Leave empty until you want GitHub Actions to collect evidence on a schedule.

github_repository_id.description: The numeric ID of the GitHub repository. See github_owner_id.

monitoring.description: Switch on the monitoring services in monitoring.tf: CloudTrail, VPC flow logs, AWS Config, and Security Hub. Together they cost a few dollars a month in an account this small.

monitoring_cloudtrail.description: Create the CloudTrail trail. Ignored when monitoring is false.

monitoring_config.description: Record every resource change with AWS Config. Ignored when monitoring is false.

monitoring_flow_logs.description: Record network traffic in SecuGuard's network. Ignored when monitoring is false.

monitoring_security_hub.description: Switch on Security Hub and its best practices standard. Ignored when monitoring is false.

planted_findings.description:
Create the deliberate weaknesses in planted.tf so the checks have real problems to
find. Every one is built to be harmless: the users and role are blocked from doing
anything, the bucket is empty, and nothing is reachable from the internet. Set to
false to remove them all.

planted_load_balancer.description: Create the load balancer with an outdated TLS policy. It costs about $17 a month while it exists. Ignored when planted_findings is false.

planted_vendor_account_id.description:
The outside AWS account that the planted vendor role trusts. AWS rejects account
numbers that do not exist, so the default is an account AWS itself owns: the one
its load balancing service uses in us-east-1, published in the AWS documentation.
The role carries a deny-everything permissions boundary, so trusting it grants nothing.
You can put a second account of your own here instead.

vpc_cidr.description: Address range for the SecuGuard VPC.
